clue.text: Dog has orange or an apple

definitions.meaning: a red-and-white breed of toy spaniel
... Orange is an old English variety of eating apple

explanation.surface: A dog owner offers a choice of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orange' tempts as the fruit or the colour, but it is part of an apple's name, Blenheim Orange; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One name serves both a spaniel breed, from the Marlborough estate, and a traditional dessert apple variety.

clue.text: Means of directing game may depend on this

definitions.text: Means of directing game may depend on this

parts.words: Means of directing game may depend on this
parts.note: the referee's whistle, which directs a game, hangs from a cord around the neck

explanation.surface: Success in a match may hinge on strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depend' means literally hang down; the means of directing the game is a whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord worn around the neck holds a whistle or knife.

definitions.meaning: a burglar who works at night

explanation.surface: A night-time thief is compared to an owl.
explanation.definitionFit: A night-time burglar and the American nightjar share the name.

clue.text: Taking food from a tin for example?

indicators.note: the letters for example come from either side, so they hold the other words inside

explanation.surface: Someone eats straight out of a can.
explanation.walkthrough: A TIN goes between E and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Consuming a meal is the act of putting food in the mouth.

parts.note: training here is going by train, not athletes' exercise in thin air

explanation.surface: Gear for athletes preparing in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training' suggests athletic preparation; it means travelling by train.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack or funicular line carries trains up steep slopes to summits.

parts.note: if a bill is met, it is paid
a hod is a scuttle or bucket for carrying coal

explanation.surface: A scheme for funding a coal delivery man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a' is a link between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A systematic way of doing something is a scheme or procedure.

clue.text: Spinster say caught barking up the wrong tree

indicators.note: say tells the solver the title for a spinster is spoken, so it is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Miss is the title for an unmarried woman, heard as the prefix mis-
taken means caught or captured

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman is captured while a dog yells.
explanation.walkthrough: MISS heard aloud gives MIS-, the prefix meaning wrongly; add TAKEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Barking up the wrong tree is an idiom for being in error.

definitions.meaning: Portia in Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice is a wealthy inheritor of her father's fortune

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean lady hoping for great things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expectations' hints at pregnancy or Dickens; it means an inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman set to inherit wealth, as Portia of Belmont does in Shakespeare.

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word sits below the other one

parts.note: a disco is a dance party
a Very light is a signal flare, so Very can stand for Light

explanation.surface: Lighting rigs at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: Revealing or finding something hidden is a discovery or exposure.

clue.text: This man is a former champion

definitions.text: This man is a former champion

parts.words: This man is a former champion
parts.note: a chess piece is a 'man', and the mounted warrior who fought as a lord's champion in medieval times gives both readings

explanation.surface: Someone points out a retired title holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the chess term for a piece, and a medieval champion was an armoured warrior on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: The chessman shaped as a horse shares its name with the armoured warriors who once fought as champions.

clue.text: In superior position after taking a flight

definitions.text: In superior position after taking a flight

parts.words: In superior position after taking a flight
parts.note: a flight here is a set of stairs, not an air journey, and superior means literally higher up

explanation.surface: Someone is promoted after a plane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests an aircraft; it means a staircase climbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbing a flight of steps puts one on a higher floor of the house.

indicators.note: resolving means breaking up and settling afresh, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An NCO sorts out a dispute in the soldiers' dining hall.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of MATTER IN, signalled by 'resolving', is spelt out; 'mess', an army dining room, only dresses the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict disciplinarian, the stereotype of a parade-ground sergeant-major.

clue.text: Able to vary act, showing reflective capacity

indicators.note: to vary means to change, so the letters of the preceding word are rearranged

parts.note: to act is to do

explanation.surface: A versatile performer's range is on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to vary' turns ABLE into ALBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Albedo is the proportion of light a surface throws back, a measure of reflectiveness.

clue.text: Publicity chap would be a lunatic on the motorway

indicators.note: the answer with the motorway letter set on it would become the lunatic, so that letter is what is taken away
the answer with the motorway letter set on it would become the lunatic, so that letter is what is taken away

parts.note: a lunatic is a madman
M, as in M1, abbreviates motorway

explanation.surface: An advertising man drives like a maniac.
explanation.walkthrough: Put M (motorway) on the front and the answer becomes MADMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An advertising executive writes and sells commercials, so he is a publicity man.

clue.text: Soldier's hat is missing on manoeuvres here

indicators.note: on manoeuvres suggests troops moving about, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: the letters of is are the ones missing from the anagram

explanation.surface: A soldier has lost his hat during army exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLDIERSHAT less I and S, rearranged, gives the answer; 'missing' signals the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: This Hampshire town is the traditional home of the British Army, where manoeuvres take place.

parts.note: a side is a party or faction in a dispute
an issue is a matter or affair under discussion

explanation.surface: A political party's scandal diverts attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter of secondary importance draws attention away from the main point.

clue.text: Turning left, like Compton Mackenzie's street

definitions.meaning: spiralling or turning to the left
Sinister Street is a 1913 novel by Compton Mackenzie

explanation.surface: Directions to a novelist's road.
explanation.definitionFit: Left-handed or anticlockwise, the Latin word sinister meaning the left side.

clue.text: Accept odd trips as fitting for sailing ship

parts.note: to bow to something is to accept it

indicators.note: odd means strange, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Agreeing to strange voyages suits a seafarer.
explanation.definitionFit: The spar projecting from a ship's bow is part of its fittings.

clue.text: Dodge by directors helps negotiate sticky situation

definitions.note: a plural noun phrase, aids for getting across mud

parts.note: to duck is to dodge
a board is a company's body of directors

explanation.surface: A firm's leaders evade trouble to escape a tricky spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticky situation' suggests a predicament, but it is literal mud.
explanation.definitionFit: Slatted wooden walkways laid over mud, as in the trenches, help people cross boggy ground.

definitions.meaning: the strongest tower of a castle
A novel by A. J. Cronin, a doctor, about a doctor

explanation.surface: Hand on a physician's volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortress or stronghold, and Cronin's novel about medicine.

definitions.meaning: time is 'the ...' in the stock phrase about running out of it

explanation.surface: A medium speaks of the afterlife and the passing of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; 'time is the enemy' is a common idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Opponents in a conflict are the foe, and time is called the foe when it runs short.

parts.note: looking-glass here is a single lens for seeing through, a toff's eyeglass

explanation.surface: A fop's mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking-glass' suggests a mirror; it means an eyeglass. Bertie Wooster is P. G. Wodehouse's upper-class idler.
explanation.definitionFit: A single eyeglass worn wedged in the eye is a stereotype of the upper-class twit.

parts.note: an S-bend has that shape
paced means measured out in strides

explanation.surface: A road curve paced out by a surveyor.
explanation.definitionFit: Things set at even distances apart are evenly separated.

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter for new is removed

parts.note: rations are fixed allowances of food

explanation.surface: Family members get no fresh pocket money.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratios express proportional relationships between quantities.

definitions.meaning: a pretender might say of himself ..., split as two words

explanation.surface: A false claimant to the throne makes a grand speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pretender' suggests a claimant to a throne; here it is just someone acting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grand and commanding is striking; split, the letters give a poser's confession.

clue.text: Likely place for an unofficial rose?

definitions.text: Likely place for an unofficial rose

parts.words: Likely place for an unofficial rose
parts.note: an unofficial rose is a wild one, like the dog rose, growing in a field boundary rather than a garden

explanation.surface: Where a rogue flower might turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unofficial' means wild, uncultivated.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild dog roses grow in the lines of shrubs bordering country fields.

clue.text: Truthfulness of no account in church office?

indicators.note: no means without, so the letters for account are removed

parts.note: accuracy is correctness or truthfulness

explanation.surface: A church post where honesty counts for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate's post is a junior clerical position in the church.

parts.note: scouts here are not boy scouts tying knots but those seeking gifted performers or players

explanation.surface: Scouts need a skill for their badges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scouts' suggests the youth movement; the scouts are talent scouts.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural aptitude is what talent scouts look for in performers and players.

parts.note: eminence here means a high peak, not fame, so the singer performs on a mountain

explanation.surface: A celebrated vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eminence' suggests fame; it means a height, an Alpine slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine herdsmen sing in a warbling falsetto on the mountainsides.
